text.p: Britain's NatWest Securities downgraded Copenhagen Airports to add from buy in a report received by Reuters on Monday.

"Following moderate outperformance last year, the shares now trade on a seven percent premium to the Danish market and the discount to sector leader British Airports Authority(BAA) has narrowed to 15 percent," NatWest said.
"We believe there is upside in the rating but the scope for further outperformance has clearly diminished, therefore we temper our recommendation from buy to add," it said.

NatWest said that the downward adjustment to add meant it expected Copenhagen Airports stock to climb between 10-20 percent more than the Danish share market, rather than over 20 percent like buy-rated paper.
"If Copenhagen Airports can reduce the discount to BAA further, the share would be close to a hold recommendation," NatWest aviation analyst Mike Powell told Reuters.

NatWest forecasts in its report that Copenhagen Airports' pre-tax profit for 1996 will be 432 million crowns, compared to 1995's 376 million crowns, rising to 456 million crowns this year and 498 million crowns in 1998.
